extracted.intended_audience: creative writers, literature students, and scholars studying James Joyce and modernist fiction
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and apply the evaluative and compositional criteria discussed in the Wikipedia article on Ulysses — i.e., criteria for assessing or emulating Joyce's novel-writing techniques (stream-of-consciousness, epiphany, symbolism, editorial fidelity, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproduction of characters' thoughts (stream-of-consciousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: "verbal method can be justified" since Joyce is "trying to reproduce the thoughts of personage"; interior monologue and "stream of consciousness" techniques are central.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Render a character's interior life directly: use interior monologue and free indirect style to reproduce the flow, vagrant and obsessive associations, and unconscious material of the mind (examples: Leopold Bloom's thoughts). Balance fidelity to mental processes with readability so the technique serves character and theme rather than becoming an unreadable display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epiphany techniques as artistic units
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of distinct "epiphany techniques" used in Ulysses, from simple revelation (e.g., a physical detail) to complex symbolic structures; the epiphany is described as "the real artistic (and dramatic) unit of Joyce's 'stream-of-consciousness' writing."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure moments of insight (epiphanies) as key narrative units. Use small revelations (a limp, a gesture) and larger, symbolic incidents (bowl symbolism) to crystallize meaning; sometimes produce 'quidditas' (essence) directly (example: Molly Bloom as 'female essence').

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish characters by what they say; evoke place not by direct description
rubrics_metrics.description: "He established his characters by what they say; and his places, named but not described, live in the minds of his characters."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show character through speech and thought rather than through authorial description. Let settings be evoked through characters' perceptions and dialogues—place becomes real via characters' engagement rather than exhaustive descriptive prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use particulars to suggest inner or general things (symbolist usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Joyce "used these particulars to suggest inner or general things—in the manner of Baudelaire and Flaubert. Such usage is symbolist; for a symbol is a common thing, closely observed, suggesting other things."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select ordinary objects and concrete details that stand for larger ideas or emotions. Close observation of common things should gesture to wider meanings; cultivate parallels and motifs that let particulars accumulate symbolic weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network of motifs, allusion, and charged words
rubrics_metrics.description: The novel's "riddling motifs" are "complicated in turn by allusion, quotation, and single images or charged words" that gradually link together to form a network binding the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weave recurring motifs, quotations, and charged images across the text to create interlocking resonances. Use allusion and carefully chosen words to build a coherent matrix of meanings rather than isolated incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity and internal logic of personages
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim that the "personages of Ulysses are not fictitious" and that they act according to some "lex eterna, an ineluctable condition of their very existence" — i.e., characters must behave according to their own inner laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure characters act from a consistent internal logic and psychological reality. Even experimental narration must preserve believable motive, habit, and pattern so characters feel authentic rather than merely symbolic or constructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise rendering of lived experience
rubrics_metrics.description: "attempts to render 'as precisely and as directly as it is possible in words to do, what our participation in life is like'" — the aim to depict moment-to-moment experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for immediacy and precision in depicting consciousness and perception. Use language to capture ephemeral, momentary experience; prioritize the textures and rhythms of lived life over telegraphic plot-summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambitious literary scope and elevation of the novel
rubrics_metrics.description: "setting the standard of the novel so high that it need not be ashamed to take its place beside poetry and drama" — the novel as an artform aspiring to the height of poetry/drama.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose with an ambition to expand the novel's possibilities: integrate poetic, dramatic, and formal resources. Strive for formal daring and aesthetic achievement that challenges genre expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and calibration of obscene/taboo material
rubrics_metrics.description: Debates over obscenity: critics call passages "obscene" or "vile," yet some argue "its very obscenity is somehow beautiful" and note Joyce "selected carefully what he puts in."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If including taboo or explicit content, be deliberate and selective: ensure such material serves artistic, thematic, or psychological purposes rather than gratuitous shock. Framing, tone, and craft can make transgressive material contribute to pity, beauty, or insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmation of ordinary life; moral calibration
rubrics_metrics.description: The observation that the work is "a book of life" in which "every sentence... seemed to have been calibrated to assert... the singularity and worth of even the most humdrum... human days."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write with an ethical/aesthetic aim to affirm the significance of everyday experience. Use detailed attention to ordinary moments to produce moral or existential resonance without melodrama.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating universal significance through microcosm
rubrics_metrics.description: "Leopold Bloom becomes a modern Ulysses, an Everyman in a Dublin which becomes a microcosm of the world."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a particular setting and particular characters as a microcosm to explore universal themes. Ground universal claims in concrete local detail to avoid abstraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parody and formal play with naturalism (catalogue of externals)
rubrics_metrics.description: The "catalogue of externals in Mr. Bloom's parlor is not naturalistic but a parody of naturalism and its reduction to absurdity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use lists, catalogs, or hyper-detailed inventories to critique or parody naturalistic representation. Formal play can expose conventions by exaggeration or inversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linguistic innovation: neologisms, truncations, and hybrid language
rubrics_metrics.description: Joyce forced language "to reproduce Joyce's fantasies in all kinds of juxtapositions, neologisms, amalgamations, truncations, words that are only found scrawled up in public lavatories, obsolete words, words in limbo or belike in the womb of time."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiment with lexical invention, archaisms, slang, and unusual juxtapositions to achieve a distinctive voice. Ensure such innovations serve expressive aims rather than merely obscuring meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textual/editorial fidelity and edition-making standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication-history disputes: first editions contained many errors; later editors (e.g., Gabler) were criticized for choices about copy-text, unnecessary changes, and following printed editions rather than manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing or using scholarly editions, distinguish authorial 'deliberate errors' from non-authorial mistakes. Justify emendations, document editorial theory (choice of copy-text, use of manuscripts vs printed sources), and avoid arbitrary changes that contradict authorial practice. Transparency and adherence to sound textual-critical methods are required.
